headline: AI Incident Database lists Incident 1846: credentials saved by an AI coding assistant reportedly reached public repositories
claim: The AI Incident Database catalogues Incident 1846: credentials saved by Anthropic's Claude Code reportedly appeared in public repositories. The incident date it records is 2026-11-02.
quote: Incident 1846: Credentials Saved by Anthropic's Claude Code AI Coding Assistant Reportedly Appeared in Public Repositories
why: A file an agent writes for convenience can carry the credentials it was given. The database says "reportedly", and so do we.
limits: The primary report the database cites (GitGuardian) was not opened, so its figures are not shown here.

headline: An open archive of AI agent security events: of 417 records, the archive says only 153 have a confirmed victim
claim: The Orca AI Incident Archive covers 2025-01 to 2026-11-08 and says that of its 417 records, only 153 have a confirmed victim.
quote: Coverage runs from 2025-01 to 2026-11-08 — 417 records of AI agent security events arranged month by month, plus one precursor traceable to 2024-12-01. Each record is a single Markdown file with a YAML header, an attack-chain diagram and at least one primary source you can click. Of the 417, only 153 have a confirmed victim.
why: No confirmed victim is not the same as no harm. Unknown is not safe.
limits: The archive records publicly disclosed events only. Its counts are the archive's own, not a census.

headline: EU publishes Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, the Digital Omnibus on AI, amending the AI Act
claim: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of 8 July 2026 amends Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act). It was published in the Official Journal on 24 July 2026.
quote: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 8 July 2026 amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, (EU) 2018/1139 and (EU) 2023/1230 as regards the simplification of the implementation of harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Digital Omnibus on AI)
why: Any date taken from the original 2024 AI Act text now has to be checked against the amendment.
limits: This item states the act exists and what it amends. It does not summarise which obligations or dates changed.

headline: EUR-Lex: the AI Act "has been changed"; the current consolidated version is dated 27/07/2026
claim: EUR-Lex marks Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as in force and changed, with a consolidated version dated 27 July 2026.
quote: In force: This act has been changed. Current consolidated version: 27/07/2026
why: Cite the consolidated text, not the 2024 original.
limits: On the same page EUR-Lex marks the Official Journal PDF as the authentic version; the consolidated text is not it.

headline: OWASP publishes the LLM Top 10 for 2026, with "Hidden Context Exposure" as LLM08
claim: The OWASP GenAI Security Project published the 2026 edition of the Top 10 for LLM Applications on 4 August 2026. LLM08:2026 is Hidden Context Exposure.
why: Sensitive Information Disclosure is LLM02 and Excessive Agency is LLM03: what an agent can reach, and what it may do with it.
limits: On 2026-11-24 the page genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/ still listed the 2025 items; the repository is the canonical source it names.

headline: MCP specification 2026-07-28 removes protocol-level sessions; every request carries its own version and capabilities
claim: The Model Context Protocol specification revision 2026-07-28 removes protocol-level sessions and the initialize handshake. Each request carries its protocol version and client capabilities, and clients SHOULD identify themselves on each request.
quote: Remove protocol-level sessions and the Mcp-Session-Id header from the Streamable HTTP transport.
why: With no session to lean on, whatever decides an agent's access has to decide it per request.
limits: "SHOULD" is a recommendation in the specification, not a requirement.

headline: OpenTelemetry's GenAI conventions, agent spans included, have moved to their own repository and are still in Development
claim: OpenTelemetry's GenAI semantic conventions moved to a dedicated repository. The agent and framework spans there are marked Status: Development.
quote: GenAI semantic conventions have moved to the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions repository.
why: Agent traces are not yet a stable standard. A trace shows what was logged, not what the agent could reach.
limits: The page gives no date for the move, so none is shown.
